sections.title: Start here
sections.tagline: Three amps on one bass, each on its own slice of the range.
sections.what: Parabola splits your bass into three bands (low, mid, high) and gives each band its own amp capture (a NAM file you load). The low band stays clean and compressed so the bottom never gets mushy; the mid band growls; the high band adds grit and fizz. Then a cab IR goes on the mid and high bands, a graphic EQ shapes the total, and it all comes back out as one signal.
sections.how: This is the trick behind parallel bass rigs like the Parallax X: distortion on the lows turns to mud, so the lows are kept clean and the drive happens above them. Parabola does the split with phase-aligned crossovers, so with nothing loaded and every band at 0 dB, your signal comes out unchanged.
sections.sound: Modern metal and djent bass: a tight, round low end that holds up the mix, with a snarling, articulate top on it, and every part adjustable on its own.
try: Put Parabola on your bass track (DI, no amp before it). It replaces your amp and cab.
Pick a starter preset (the PRESET bar): it finds its captures by file name in your tones folders.
Or open MY GEAR and click captures to load them into bands, and an IR into the cab.
Hover anything: the bar at the bottom says what it does. Drop .nam files right onto the bands.
controls: < and > step through them, click the name for the list, SAVE stores yours, DEL deletes yours.
Every capture and IR in your tones folders, one click to load.
Silences noise between notes, on your DI before everything. Fully down is off.
Transposes everything ±12 semitones before the bands.
Level into Parabola and out of it, ±24 dB. The meter turns red when the output clips.
Opens the tuner and mutes the output.
Settings: the skin, and in the standalone app your audio interface and latency.

sections.title: Presets
sections.tagline: A whole rig, captures included, in one click.
sections.what: A preset stores every knob plus which capture is in each band and which IR is on the cab. The starter presets are built around free TONE3000 captures (an Ampeg SVT-CL pack, a Darkglass B7K pack, the Darkglass Alpha Omega and Microtubes 500 packs) and three cab IR packs. Your own presets save alongside them.
sections.how: Captures are saved by file name and last location. Loading a preset looks in the saved location first, then for a file with the same name anywhere in your tones folders (Documents\Parabola Bass Z, Documents\T3KJ Tones and any folder you added in My Gear, subfolders included). Anything it can't find is named in the hint bar, and that band is left empty. Your presets live in %APPDATA%\Parabola Bass Z\presets.json.
sections.sound: Starter presets: Djent Low End, Modern Growl, Fuzz Wall, Alpha Omega Split, Vintage Round, Clean DI + Grit, Microtubes Clean, and Init (empty).
try: Click the preset name and pick Djent Low End.
Tweak it, click SAVE, type a name, press Enter.
Use < and > to flip through presets while you play.
controls: Click for the list: STARTER and YOURS.
Saves the current settings and captures as your preset (Enter to save, Esc to cancel). Same name = replace.
Deletes the current preset (yours only). Click twice.

sections.title: My Gear
sections.tagline: Your captures and IRs, one click away.
sections.what: A list of every capture (.nam) and IR (.wav, .aiff, .flac) in your tones folders, grouped by the folder they're in, with search. Keep your captures wherever you like: add that folder once with FOLDERS.
sections.how: It reads Documents\Parabola Bass Z, Documents\T3KJ Tones (T3KJ's My Gear folder) and any folder you add with FOLDERS (subfolders included), so nothing needs a second copy. Click a capture, then pick LOW, MID or HIGH. Click an IR and it goes straight onto the cab.
sections.sound: Quick A/B-ing: keep My Gear open and swap the mid band's capture until the growl sits right.
try: Click MY GEAR, then FOLDERS > Add a folder, and pick the folder you unzip captures into (C:\Users\you\NAM Tones (Bass), say).
Type 'b7k' in the search box, click B7K Djent, pick MID.
Added files? Click RESCAN.
controls: Add a folder to look in, or remove one you added. Presets search them too.
Opens Documents\Parabola Bass Z (and makes NAMs and Cabs inside it).

sections.title: Crossover
sections.tagline: Where the low band ends and the drive begins.
sections.what: The display shows the three bands as colored curves, including each band's level and EQ. The two white handles are the split points: Low / Mid (default 180 Hz) and Mid / High (default 1.6 kHz).
sections.how: Each split is a Linkwitz-Riley 24 dB/octave filter pair, the standard for speaker crossovers because the two sides add back up flat. The low band also passes through a matching all-pass, so all three bands stay in phase with each other.
sections.sound: A higher Low / Mid split keeps more of the bass clean (rounder, more polite). A lower one lets the drive reach further down (meaner, but watch for mud). The Mid / High split decides how much of the growl is 'mid' versus 'fizz'.
try: Start at 180 Hz / 1.6 kHz. For 5-string or drop tunings try 150 Hz.
Mute the mid and high bands (their power lights) to hear just the low band, then sweep Low / Mid.
Double-click a handle to put it back to its default.
controls: Drag left or right: 60 to 400 Hz.
Drag left or right: 600 Hz to 5 kHz.
Each band's level, or OFF when its power light is off.

sections.title: Low band
sections.what: Everything below the Low / Mid split. It can run a capture (a clean amp is the classic choice) or nothing at all for a pure DI low end, then goes through its own compressor.
sections.how: Drive sets the level into the capture. Comp is a one-knob compressor: turning it up lowers the threshold and raises the ratio, with a little makeup gain, so the lows sit at an even level whatever you play. By default the low band skips the cab IR, the Parallax way: a cab would only smear the fundamental.
sections.sound: The weight and the pitch of every note: solid, even, never fuzzy.
try: Leave it empty, or load a clean amp (an Ampeg SVT clean, say). Comp around 40%.
More Comp for picked, aggressive parts; less for fingerstyle dynamics.
ADV: a little Bass boost here instead of in the graphic EQ keeps the drive bands tight.
controls: Load a .nam capture (or drop one on the band), or remove it.
Level into the capture, -12 to +24 dB.
The band's volume in the mix.
Shelf at 100 Hz, bell at 650 Hz, shelf at 3 kHz, ±12 dB.
Send this band through the cab IR. Off by default for low.

sections.title: Mid band
sections.what: Between the two splits: where a bass's character and most of its distortion live. Load a drive capture here (a Darkglass-style pedal or a driven amp).
sections.how: Drive pushes the band harder into its capture. Each capture's output is level-matched from its loudness data, so swapping captures doesn't jump the volume. Tone is a low-pass after the capture that rounds off the top of the distortion. Through the cab IR by default.
sections.sound: Growl, bark and definition: what makes a riff audible in a dense mix.
try: Load B7K Djent or B7K Hard Rock. Drive 0 dB to start, then up to taste.
Tone around 5 kHz keeps the growl without fizz; open it up if the high band is off.
Level a couple of dB under the low band is a good starting balance.
controls: Load a .nam capture (or drop one on the band), or remove it.
How hard the capture is pushed, -12 to +24 dB.
Low-pass after the capture, 1 to 20 kHz (fully up is off).
The band's volume in the mix.
Shelf at 100 Hz, bell at 650 Hz, shelf at 3 kHz, ±12 dB.
Send this band through the cab IR. On by default.

sections.title: High band
sections.what: Everything above the Mid / High split: string noise, pick attack and the fizzy edge of a distorted bass. A heavier drive capture usually goes here.
sections.how: Same as the mid band: Drive into the capture, level-matched output, a Tone low-pass, Bass / Mid / Treble, then the cab IR. Because only the top of the range reaches this capture, you can drive it very hard without the low end turning to mush.
sections.sound: The aggressive top end metal bass is known for. A little goes a long way; it's usually the quietest band.
try: Load B7K Heavy or B7K Distortion. Level around -6 dB.
Tone at 8 to 12 kHz takes the harsh edge off.
Mute it and unmute it: the difference is how 'modern' the tone sounds.
controls: Load a .nam capture (or drop one on the band), or remove it.
How hard the capture is pushed, -12 to +24 dB.
Low-pass after the capture, 1 to 20 kHz (fully up is off).

sections.title: Cab
sections.tagline: A speaker cabinet for the drive bands.
sections.what: Load a cab impulse response (a .wav) and it's applied to every band whose CAB switch is on: mid and high by default. The top line says which bands go through it.
sections.how: The IR is convolved (zero added latency) with the sum of the cab bands. A capture whose file says it already includes a cab (a 'full rig' capture, like the Alpha Omega pack) skips the IR automatically, so it isn't doubled up.
sections.sound: The cab takes the raw fizz off the distortion and gives it the shape of a real speaker. 8x10s are big and round, 4x10s tighter and punchier, 2x15s warm and vintage.
try: Try an Ampeg 8x10 with a D6 mic, then an Eden 4x10, and compare.
CAB ON off for a DI-style tone (with a guitar-style cab sim later in the chain, say).
Drag a .wav straight onto the cab panel.
controls: Load an IR (.wav, .aiff, .flac) or remove it.
Runs the cab bands through the IR. Off bypasses it for every band.

sections.title: Graphic EQ
sections.tagline: Final shaping, after the bands are back together.
sections.what: Six faders, ±12 dB, at 80 Hz, 250 Hz, 500 Hz, 1 kHz, 2.5 kHz and 6 kHz, on the mixed signal.
sections.how: Six bell filters in a row. A fader at 0 dB is switched out completely.
sections.sound: 80 Hz is the thump, 250 Hz the boom (cut it for clarity), 500 Hz the wood, 1 kHz the honk and clank, 2.5 kHz the growl and attack, 6 kHz the sizzle.
try: Cut 250 Hz by 2 to 4 dB to clean up mud.
Boost 1 kHz or 2.5 kHz a little to cut through guitars.
Double-click a fader to reset it.
controls: Drag up to boost, down to cut. Double-click resets.

sections.title: Captures & IRs
sections.what: Parabola doesn't ship with any captures or IRs: you load your own .nam files (from TONE3000, say) and cab IRs. Their licenses usually don't allow passing the files around, so each person downloads their own.
sections.how: Parabola remembers each band's file and the IR by their location on your computer, so a project or a saved session finds them again as long as they stay put. Put them in Documents\Parabola Bass Z\NAMs and \Cabs (the installer makes those folders) and the LOAD buttons open there.
sections.sound: Good starting points: a clean Ampeg SVT for low, a Darkglass B7K pack for mid and high, an Ampeg 8x10 or Eden 4x10 IR.
try: Download captures, drop them into Documents\Parabola Bass Z\NAMs (or keep them in T3KJ Tones).
Open MY GEAR and click one to load it, or drag a .nam onto a band.
The starter presets look for specific packs by file name: see Presets.
controls: A capture with a cab in it. Parabola skips the IR for it.
Every capture is brought to the same loudness, from its own data.

sections.title: Pitch & Tuner
sections.tagline: Drop-tune without touching the pegs, and tune silently.
sections.what: Pitch transposes your whole signal up or down, in semitones, before the bands, so a 4-string in E can play like it's in D or B. TUNER opens a tuner and mutes the output while it's open.
sections.how: Pitch uses T3KJ's pitch shifter (a correlation-spliced delay line that keeps even low B clean and re-syncs on every pick attack). While Pitch isn't 0 it adds about 16 ms of delay, which Parabola reports to your DAW. The tuner listens to your DI before anything else.
sections.sound: -2 for drop D-style riffs on a standard-tuned bass, -5 for a B-standard feel. Bigger shifts get more artificial.
try: Set Pitch to -2 and play an open E: you'll hear a D.
Click TUNER, play each open string, close it when they're green.
controls: Note, cents and Hz; green when within 3 cents. Output muted while open.

sections.title: MIDI & footswitches
sections.tagline: Put any control on a footswitch or pedal.
sections.what: Every knob, power light, CAB switch and EQ fader can follow a MIDI CC from a controller (a Quad Cortex footswitch, an expression pedal).
sections.how: Right-click a control, choose MIDI Learn, then press the footswitch or move the pedal. Switches follow the CC (64 and up is on). Mappings save with the plugin's state. In a DAW you can also use its own parameter learn. The standalone app needs your controller ticked under MIDI inputs in its audio settings.
sections.sound: Footswitch the high band on for choruses, or put the mid band's Drive on an expression pedal.
try: Right-click the HIGH power light, MIDI Learn, press a footswitch.
Right-click it again to forget the CC.
controls: Shows a control's CC once it's mapped.

sections.title: Settings & latency
sections.what: The gear opens Settings: five skins (Foil, Inferno, Hologram, Ram, Ember), and in the standalone app your audio interface, input, outputs, sample rate and buffer, with a latency readout.
sections.how: Captures are trained at 48 kHz, so Parabola runs everything at 48 kHz. If your project or interface runs at another rate, it converts on the way in and out, which adds under 1 ms; it tells your DAW so tracks stay lined up. At 48 kHz it adds nothing.
sections.sound: For the lowest latency: ASIO, 48 kHz, and the smallest buffer that doesn't crackle (64 or 128 is typical). Three captures use more CPU than one; raise the buffer if it crackles.
try: No sound in the standalone app? Turn on Hear yourself and check your bass's input is ticked.
Drag the bottom-right corner to resize the window (60% to 200%).
controls: The photo and colors. Saved with the plugin's state.
Plays the output while your input is live. Off by default to prevent feedback.
